headline: Highest risk is data leakage: gpt-researcher can read files and use broad egress, while system_prompts_leaks is a docs-only, non-runnable source-available repo with no runtime protections documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read filesystem content and use MCP/browser workflows, so if system_prompts_leaks content is placed in a shared workspace or copied into its inputs, prompt-like text could influence it. The pair has no documented isolation or provenance tracking, and the B profile is a prompt-leak repository, so interaction risk is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same workspace or copied text channel
IF system_prompts_leaks content is treated as instructions rather than inert data
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Strip instruction-like text before passing files between agents
Use a human review step for any copied prompts
Disable MCP sharing between the agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents and secrets and has broad network egress, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and could expose prompt material if shared through files or copied outputs. No shared filesystem is documented, but the pair lacks explicit data-handling boundaries, so leakage is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF local documents or secrets are placed into a shared folder
IF gpt-researcher sends retrieved content to external APIs during the same task
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Run gpt-researcher on a separate account

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can install packages, spawn subprocesses, and read files, but system_prompts_leaks is not runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-side interaction, so conflict severity stays low.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks is wrapped in a separate executable harness with write access
IF both agents are granted the same mutable directory by an external orchestrator
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access
Run the non-runnable repo only as static content

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that can generate citations and reports, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak corpus that could be treated as source material. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors or misleading claims can cascade into polished but untrusted research artifacts.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher outputs are used as authoritative source text
IF downstream consumers accept the resulting report without independent verification

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not runnable; the main compliance issue is accidental exposure of sensitive research data into a public repo or public-facing corpus. The B agent is the only one clearly tied to public distribution, so it is the primary citation here.
conditions: IF PHI, regulated data, or secrets are copied into system_prompts_leaks content
IF the resulting artifacts are published or shared externally
